author: _shemnon
content: The reason for 3 precompiles is to add all 3 strengths.  Some regulators are cool with ML-DSA-44, some want ML-DSA-65, and some are even requiring ML-DSA-87.  There is agreement on the algorithm, but the strength varies based on the country. The alternate is all three strengths in one precompile, but the logic is simpler if it's fixed algo not switched algo.

author: _shemnon
content:
Going stronger just means bigger keys and signatures, no other restrictions.  It's not like P384 where the math wasn't friendly to the 256 bit registers and couldn't be done in-evm well (EVM384, pepridge farms remembers). 

One thing to note is that the ML-DSA digests are over the whole message, not a hash like ECDSA sigs.  However I expect auth sigs will be over the TXHash and I think that's fine, but a general purpose signer should support arbitrary message length (modulo gas)

author: kevaundray
content:
I'm still not sure we should add the same precompile with three different strengths.

Consider the case where 90% of usage is with ml-dsa-44 and the other 10% is with the other two. 
I don't think we would/should add the other two in such a case because there is a cost to adding precompiles to the protocol

author: _shemnon
content: The problem is US regulators want the weaker one, and australians want the stronger one, and security bits are getting shaved, so -44 could fall off from use in 5 years (it may not as well).  There is already diverance between other chains, BNB and tron is movng towards -44 and near, canton has -65. Australia is moving towards requiring -78 for retail banks.

author: kevaundray
content: If -44 falls off from use in five years, then we would deprecate the precompile and all contracts who switched to it would need to change?

author: _shemnon
content: similar to ECDSA, that's why contracts that do on-chain signature validation need to have a durable solution. from my perspective very little has been done to contemplate what PQC migrations means to contracts. Part of that is because they don't know what the EVM surface will look like, or not look like.

author: _shemnon
content: the ssz multi-algo solution (secondary signatures) had a composite precompile at one point, but that is encoding algorithm ids to the contract and transactions, still requiring in-protocol coordination for algorithm additions/removals.
